html:
A town on the lagoon in southeastern Benin, the seat of a small kingdom of Gun and Yoruba people, rival of Dahomey, whose king accepted a French protectorate in 1863 to defend himself.

Its name, new port, was given by Portuguese slave traders. The French alliance brought them into the region, leading to the Franco-Dahomean Wars. Porto-Novo became the capital of the French colony of Dahomey and is still the official capital of Benin, though the government sits mostly in Cotonou. Afro-Brazilian returnees built its Great Mosque in the style of a Brazilian church. See also de Souza.
